first.rationale: Verify the two most consequential, decision-relevant beliefs: whether onboarding simplification can reverse the current completion and activation declines, and whether targeted pricing would protect qualified revenue against the competitor. I currently intend to test simplified onboarding because it addresses both observed funnel deteriorations and is more likely to produce sustainable value than broad discounting. Pricing could still be warranted for a narrowly defined segment if verification confirms durable revenue quality.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, given confirmed gains in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. This directly addresses the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not prioritize promotional pricing: although it increased short-term qualified revenue, the 12% retention decline indicates poor renewal durability. Monitor activation, completion, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention as guardrails.

final2.rationale: Run a narrowly targeted, retention-gated pricing test for genuinely price-sensitive SMB accounts facing competitor pressure, rather than broadening discounts. The verified evidence shows acquisition and short-term qualified-revenue gains but a 12% 30-day retention decline and poor first-renewal durability. Set strict renewal, gross-margin, and qualified-revenue guardrails; stop if retention deterioration repeats. Continue treating onboarding simplification as the sustainable funnel intervention, but it is unlikely to address this immediate price-driven churn spike.
